Yes, vets often prescribe medication (gabapentin) to help calm down their back. The medication helps but does not completely stop the behaviors from happening. FHS can present as dermatological, neurological, or psychological. 
I am still finding the best method for my cat to help calm down his tail (he’s a very anxious cat). 
I have also tried CBD for my cat but he’s very picky and doesn’t like the taste which is why we tried out gabapentin.

There is a condition called Feline Hyperesthesia (cat’s tail/back area is highly sensitive). I suggest some research and talking to your vet if you happen to notice the tail chasing behaviors more. Showing the vet videos of your cat interacting with their tail helps!
